episode_title: Episode #21: Q4 Isn't One Season: How We Prepare For The Changing Demand

real_qa.q: When should businesses start preparing for Q4 demand based on search trends and customer behavior?
real_qa.r: You need to look at when demand actually spikes through Google Trends and Google Search Console seasonality data, not assume people shop in November or December. For example, Christmas catering bookings peak in January for that year's events, and wedding season searches spike earlier than summer. You must then walk back the sales cycle to understand how long conversion takes, so you can start building pages and running ads at the right time—potentially months before the actual purchase period.
real_qa.requete: when to start Q4 marketing planning seasonality

real_qa.q: Why should businesses avoid automatically increasing PPC budgets in Q4 if demand is higher?
real_qa.r: More budget does not automatically mean more sales. With platforms like Google and Meta, increased spend often just raises your bid for the same limited audience without proportionally increasing conversions. If your cost per acquisition is £20, doubling budget could double that cost while not generating additional revenue. Instead, look at last year's sales, set a finite profit-based projection (perhaps 10-20% growth), and determine the actual budget needed—not what the platforms encourage you to spend.
real_qa.requete: should you increase PPC budget Q4

real_qa.q: What SEO strategy should brands use for seasonal content like Black Friday and Christmas pages?
real_qa.r: Create seasonal pages like Black Friday or Christmas guides once and reuse them year after year without dating them (don't call it 'Black Friday 2026'). Keep them live but not in main navigation year-round. Focus on creating brand-specific seasonal pages like 'domain.com/coupons-discounts' because people search for 'brand name coupons discounts' in Q4, and you'll rank better than generic coupon sites. Also create gift guides and listicles for internal linking, but be aware that AI-generated content in these areas may not rank as well for your own products because customers seek third-party validation.
real_qa.requete: Black Friday Christmas SEO seasonal pages strategy

real_qa.q: How does event-based seasonality affect Q4 marketing for food and hospitality businesses?
real_qa.r: For event-driven businesses like catering and premium food, demand is tied to occasions like Mother's Day, Father's Day, Valentine's Day, and Christmas—not just Q4. Quiet months like July, August, and September have no major events, so conversely, luxury food items sell better around events while impulse buys like barbecues remain slower. This means Q4 prep actually starts in Q3 for Christmas catering since bookings happen months in advance, making Q4 ad spend inefficient if the client is already booked.
real_qa.requete: event based seasonality catering food business

real_qa.q: How can sofa and furniture retailers differentiate during Q4 without relying on heavy discounts?
real_qa.r: Instead of competing on price with industry-wide sales, identify a unique selling point—for example, UK-manufactured sofas that can reduce lead time from 4-6 weeks to 2 weeks for select products, or pre-made stock ready to ship immediately. Work backwards from the busy period to determine what product offerings you can feasibly deliver, then build your ads and marketing around that differentiation rather than joining the crowded discount race.

guest.bio_context: Zoe Ashbridge is co-founder of Frank Marketing and co-host of the Frank Marketing Podcast. She specializes in SEO strategy and works with B2B and B2C clients on seasonal demand planning, content optimization, and search engine visibility.
